what: highlight "On the evening of August 15, 1971, Nixon addressed the nation on a new economic policy"
said: On the evening of Sunday, August fifteenth, nineteen seventy-one, millions of Americans turned on their televisions. The President had an announcement.

what: highlight "On Sunday, August 15, when American financial markets were closed"
said: He chose a Sunday on purpose. American financial markets were closed, so nobody could panic and trade until the next morning.

what: highlight "a system of national fiat currencies has been used globally"
said: Since that night, almost every country in the world has used money backed by nothing but trust. Economists call it fiat money.

what: highlight "Money used because of government decree."
said: Fiat is a Latin word. It means, let it be done. Fiat money is money because a government says it is.

what: highlight "meaning that it must be accepted in payment of a debt in specific circumstances"
said: It is also legal tender. That means, by law, it must be accepted to pay a debt.

what: highlight "hashed out by forty-four nations in Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, during July 1944"
said: Forty-four countries met at a hotel in Bretton Woods, New Hampshire. They agreed on a new system for the world's money.

what: highlight "From 1944 to 1971, the Bretton Woods agreement fixed the value of 35 United States dollars to one troy ounce of gold."
said: Other currencies would be tied to the US dollar. And the dollar would be tied to gold, at thirty-five dollars an ounce.

what: highlight "This dilemma was identified in the 1960s by Belgian-American economist Robert Triffin ."
said: But the system had a hidden flaw. An economist named Robert Triffin spotted it in the nineteen sixties.

what: highlight "the supply of dollar reserves held abroad exceeded the US stock of gold"
said: But the more dollars went abroad, the less believable the gold promise became. There simply was not enough gold for all those dollars.

what: highlight "an ounce of gold could be exchanged for US$40 in the London market"
said: In the private gold market in London, people started paying more than the official price. By nineteen sixty, an ounce cost forty dollars there, not thirty-five.

what: highlight "sent a ship to New York City to retrieve French gold deposits"
said: By the summer of nineteen seventy-one, countries were lining up. France sent a ship to New York to take its gold home.

what: highlight "Britain requested $3 billion in gold be moved from Fort Knox"
said: Days later, Britain asked for three billion dollars in gold to be moved from Fort Knox. That was the final straw.

what: highlight "as its key mechanism for temporarily defending"
said: For years, the Federal Reserve had been using special deals with other central banks, called currency swaps, to quietly defend the dollar. They were not enough anymore.

what: highlight "met secretly at Camp David to discuss policy solutions to the growing crisis"
said: On the afternoon of Friday, August thirteenth, Nixon took his top advisers to Camp David, the presidential retreat in the woods of Maryland.

what: highlight "From August 13 to 15, 1971, Nixon and fifteen advisers"
said: With him were Fed chairman Arthur Burns, Treasury Secretary John Connally, and a young Treasury official named Paul Volcker. Remember that last name.

what: highlight "was the primary political force behind them"
said: Connally was the strongest voice in the room. He wanted bold action, and he got it.

what: highlight "imposing a 90-day freeze on wages and prices"
said: Second, freeze wages and prices across the whole country for ninety days. Nobody could raise prices, and nobody could get a raise.

what: highlight "This was the first time the U.S. government had enacted wage and price controls since the Korean War."
said: It was the first time the government had controlled wages and prices since the Korean War.

what: highlight "Nixon instituted a 10 percent import surcharge"
said: Third, put an extra ten percent tax on many imported goods. That would make foreign cars and TVs more expensive, and push other countries to make a deal.

what: highlight "a looming gold run and the domestic problem of inflation"
said: They had two problems to solve at once. A run on America's gold abroad, and rising inflation at home.

what: highlight "We must protect the position of the American dollar as a pillar of monetary stability around the world."
said: Nixon told Americans he had to protect the dollar. He said it was a pillar of stability around the world.

what: highlight "your dollar will be worth just as much tomorrow as it is today"
said: If you buy a foreign car or travel abroad, he said, your dollar might buy slightly less. But if you buy American-made products, your dollar will be worth just as much tomorrow as it is today.

what: highlight "its largest daily gain ever at that point"
said: And at first, most of America agreed. The next day, the Dow jumped thirty-three points, its biggest one-day gain ever at that point.

what: highlight "We unhesitatingly applaud the boldness with which the President has moved."
said: Even the New York Times praised him. It wrote that it unhesitatingly applauded the boldness of the President.

what: highlight "Nixon was re-elected president in 1972 by a historic lan"
said: The next year, Nixon was re-elected in one of the biggest landslides in American history.

what: highlight "Meeting in December 1971 at the Smithsonian Institution in Washington D.C."
said: In December nineteen seventy-one, the world's finance ministers met at the Smithsonian Institution in Washington to patch the system.

what: highlight "the USD rate lost 7.9%"
said: America agreed to a new official gold price of thirty-eight dollars. That made the dollar worth almost eight percent less.

what: highlight "Yen +16.9%"
said: Other countries had to make their money stronger against the dollar. The Japanese yen went up almost seventeen percent.

what: highlight "a 10% devaluation was announced on 14 February 1973"
said: The patch did not hold. In February nineteen seventy-three, America cut the dollar's value by another ten percent.

what: highlight "Japan and European nations abandoned the fixed rates and allowed their currencies to float"
said: After that, Japan and the European countries gave up and let their currencies float. Floating means the price of a currency moves every day, like the price of anything else.

what: highlight "with all industrialized states following suit within a decade"
said: Within about ten years, every big industrial country was doing the same.

what: highlight "Lasting from 1965 to 1982"
said: Economists call the years from nineteen sixty-five to nineteen eighty-two the Great Inflation.

what: highlight "In 1964, inflation measured a little more than 1 percent per year."
said: In nineteen sixty-four, prices were rising only a little more than one percent a year. Barely noticeable.

what: highlight "reached more than 14 percent in 1980"
said: By nineteen eighty, inflation was above fourteen percent. In March of that year, it hit close to fifteen.

what: highlight "the separation of the US dollar from its last link to gold"
said: The Federal Reserve's own historians say the Great Inflation is partly the story of the dollar losing its last link to gold.

what: highlight "sought a reassuring, qualified nominee who would confront inflation head-on"
said: In August nineteen seventy-nine, President Jimmy Carter chose Paul Volcker to run the Federal Reserve.

what: highlight "a swollen money supply presented a grave inflationary threat"
said: Even as a college student, Volcker had written that too much money in the economy was a serious danger. Now he could act on it.

what: highlight "to a peak of 20% in June 1981"
said: His plan was painful. He pushed interest rates higher than anyone had seen. The Fed's key rate hit twenty percent in June nineteen eighty-one.

what: highlight "which had averaged 11.2% in 1979"
said: For comparison, that same rate had averaged about eleven percent in nineteen seventy-nine. Volcker nearly doubled it.

what: highlight "the national unemployment rate rose to over 10%"
said: It helped cause a deep recession. Unemployment rose above ten percent. Millions of families felt the pain.

what: highlight "widely credited with having ended the high levels of inflation"
said: But it worked. Volcker is widely credited with ending the high inflation of the nineteen seventies and early eighties.

what: highlight "In 1983, the percentage change from a year ago settled back to pre-Great Inflation levels"
said: By nineteen eighty-three, yearly inflation was back to the normal range of zero to five percent. The Great Inflation was over.

what: highlight "It eventually declined to average only 3.5 percent in the latter half of the 1980s."
said: By nineteen eighty-three, yearly inflation was back to the normal range of zero to five percent. The Great Inflation was over.

what: highlight "gold prices increased above $4,000 per troy ounce for the first time"
said: Here is one way to see it. In nineteen seventy-one, an ounce of gold officially cost thirty-five dollars. In October twenty twenty-five, it rose above four thousand dollars.

what: highlight "its permanent transformation from a creditor to a debtor nation"
said: The end of the gold link also changed America's place in the world. By nineteen eighty-five, the country had gone from being the world's lender to being a borrower.
